must_fix.issue: Stacked hedging in the early sections ('In Arab weddings generally ... is described as ... though that account is framed around ...') reads like footnotes, not a guide. Raised by planner_couple (primary, top-3 change), uhnw, search_visitor and funding_parent (the crowning source stack). r2 line 35: "The tulbeh (also written tulba, toulbe or tolbe) is the formal request for the bride's hand. In Arab weddings generally, it is described as a private visit limited to relatives: once both families have agreed to the couple's decision, the groom and his family ask the bride and her family, and the families then formally recognise that the couple will marry. <!-- fact_08 -->"; line 37: "Coffee is often told as part of the visit. In Arab weddings generally, the families reading the Fatiha after the father agrees is described as typically accompanied by Arabic coffee in the Levant, though that account is framed around Muslim families in Egypt, Palestine and Jordan rather than Lebanon. <!-- fact_10 --> Treat the details as your family's to decide."; line 41: "The engagement is the khutbeh (printed khutubah in some sources). <!-- fact_09 --> In Arab weddings generally, engagements are described as usually taking place at a simpler party or family dinner, without a zaffeh, and the couple exchange rings, placing them on each other's right-hand ring finger. <!-- fact_09 -->"; line 49: "The henna night, laylat al-henna, is a pre-wedding evening that many families keep. In Arab weddings generally, it is described as having changed over time: historically, in accounts from Palestine, the groom's family danced through the village to the bride's house, where henna was mixed and applied to the couple's hands. <!-- fact_15 --> Today, especially outside Palestine, it is described as closer to a women's celebration with music, food and dancing, and henna drawn on the palms and feet of the bride and her guests. <!-- fact_15 -->"; also lines 77 and 79 (katb al-kitab: "In Arab weddings generally it is described as the focus of the official ceremony" and "In the Levant, it is described as usually held at the bride's or groom's family home").
must_fix.fix: One framing line per section, then plain sentences. Keep every fact comment and keep the attribution honest. Example for the tulbeh: open with "Most written accounts describe Arab weddings across the region rather than Lebanon alone, so read this as the common pattern and let your families fill in their own." then "The tulbeh (also written tulba, toulbe or tolbe) is the formal request for the bride's hand: a private visit, limited to relatives, in which the groom and his family ask the bride and her family once both families have agreed, and the families then formally recognise that the couple will marry. <!-- fact_08 -->" For line 37 keep the source scope visible in one clause: "Arabic coffee is often part of the visit. One account, written about Muslim families in Egypt, Palestine and Jordan, has the families read the Fatiha once the father agrees, typically over Arabic coffee in the Levant. <!-- fact_10 --> Treat the details as your family's to decide." Engagement (line 41), henna (line 49) and katb al-kitab (lines 77, 79): drop the repeated 'In Arab weddings generally ... is described as' and state the fact plainly under that section's single framing line; keep 'in accounts from Palestine' and 'especially outside Palestine' because they limit the claim. No new facts, no new sources.
